title: Grand Trunk Road (Uttarapath, Sadak-e-Azam)
summary: The Grand Trunk Road is a long highway across the Indian subcontinent linking Afghanistan, Pakistan, India and Bangladesh. India's UNESCO tentative-list entry traces it to a Mauryan route called Uttarapath and says the first tangible remains of an integrated highway belong to the Sur period (1540-1556 CE), when Sher Shah Suri is popularly credited with rebuilding it, with sarais and kos minars. The Grand Trunk name dates from British rule.

uncertainty.note: UNESCO's tentative-list entry dates the Sur-dynasty highway to 1540-1556 CE and the Mauryan Uttarapath to the 4th-2nd century BCE, so the start is uncertain by definition of the road; the earliest connection is said to be pre-historic. End is the present: the road is in use.

as_recorded.value: Mauryan period (4 th – 2 nd Century BCE)

when.display: Highway from the Sur period (1540); older route

where.modern_name: Grand Trunk Road, Afghanistan, Pakistan, India, Bangladesh (pin: Moti Gate of Sher Shah Suri and Kos Minar, Delhi)
where.historical_name: Sadak-e-Azam (Great Road) under the Sur dynasty, running Kabul to Sonargaon

importance.justification: India's UNESCO tentative-list entry calls it one of Asia's oldest and longest roads.

reviewer_note: No model: a road has no sourced height. The pin is one listed site on the road (the Moti Gate of Sher Shah Suri and Kos Minar at Babarpur Bazipur, Delhi, N28 41 16 E77 16 50 in the UNESCO list), not the road itself, so uncertainty_km is large. UNESCO says Sur-period routes ran Kabul to Sonargaon, British-period Kabul to Chittagong; the GlobalSecurity text, quoting an older gazetteer, says Kabul to Calcutta, about 1,500 miles. Claims that Chandragupta Maurya or Ashoka built it were not stated on the opened pages and are left out.
